subject: Exportability & evidence-delivery timeline — tamper-evidence and handoff SLAs
messages:
From: contracts@trintech.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: exportability/tamper-evidence questions

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for the materials in the packet. A few quick clarifying questions from our side so we can scope the legal/technical review:

1) Retention windows: please confirm the retention tiers you offer for audit logs and custody records (hot/warm/cold) and the maximum retention you can contract to (we're evaluating 7 years as a requirement).

2) Export formats & fidelity: we need event-level exports that preserve ISO timestamps, actor identifiers, and any associated request/response payloads (where applicable). What export formats do you support (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV)? Do you include a schema for each export?

3) Tamper-evidence: for compliance we require tamper-evident delivery. Can Redwood provide signed manifests (SHA256), timestamping, or notarization? Who signs the manifest (customer key vs Redwood key)?

4) Delivery SLA & transfer options: expected delivery lead times for full archive extracts (50M events) vs smaller slices, and supported delivery mechanisms (S3 presigned, SFTP, encrypted courier).

5) Legal hold & preservation: ability to freeze deletion/retention policies for a subset of records on request, and proof of preservation.

If you can reply with concise answers and any sample manifest/export files, we can move this into our contract review.

Thanks,
Kathy Li
Contracts Manager — TrinTech
contracts@trintech.com

Attachment: registry_request_form.pdf (pdf)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: contracts@trintech.com, kathy.li@trintech.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: exportability/tamper-evidence questions

Kathy — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; happy to follow up with a short call to walk through examples.

1) Retention tiers: default platform tiers are: hot (raw ingest, 90 days), warm (indexed/aggregates, 2 years), cold archive (compressed, up to 7 years). We can contract for a maximum of 7 years for audit logs and provide a custom retention clause beyond that with enterprise pricing. Legal-hold can pin objects and prevent deletion across tiers.

2) Export formats & fidelity: supported export formats are NDJSON (event-per-line, with ISO8601 timestamps), Parquet (columnar) and CSV (for summary exports). Each export includes a machine-readable schema (JSON Schema) and a field-level manifest describing whether payloads are redacted or tokenized. We include actor IDs and request/response bodies by default unless the customer requires redaction.

3) Tamper-evidence: we deliver a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums for each exported file. Redwood can sign the manifest using our HSM-backed key and optionally include a detached signature you can verify. For higher assurance we can timestamp the manifest with a third-party timestamping authority or include a notarization step (additional cost). We also support providing a customer-supplied signing key (via KMS/HSM) so the manifest is signed by your key.

4) Delivery SLA & transfer options: typical delivery timeline for full archives (tens of millions of events) is 5–10 business days depending on size and export filters. Smaller slices (<= 5M events) are usually available within 48–72 hours. Delivery mechanisms: S3 presigned URLs to a Redwood-managed bucket, cross-account S3 transfer, SFTP over SSH with key exchange, or physical courier (encrypted drive) for very large datasets. We provide MD5/SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest on delivery.

5) Legal hold & preservation: we can place a scoped legal hold on accounts or on specific query slices. Holds are logged with an audit trail and cannot be removed without dual-approval (owner + legal contact). We produce a preservation certificate and chain-of-custody record on request.

Attached: Evidence_Manifest_v1.xlsx (manifest stub), export_sample.ndjson (sample export, 3 events), signed_manifest.sha256 (detached signature stub)

If that aligns, can we schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk the procurement/legal team through the export sample and sign-off steps?

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: kathy.li@trintech.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-04-14T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: exportability/tamper-evidence questions — technical addendum

Kathy — adding the technical specifics you requested and attaching a tiny sample of the export and schema. See below: 

Retention lock (WORM): Redwood supports configurable immutability on exported archives when written to our cold-store. For enterprise customers we can place objects in a retention lock state (non-rewritable) for the contracted retention period; this is enforced at the storage layer and reflected in the chain-of-custody certificate.

Customer-supplied signing key: we support customer-managed keys via cross-account AWS KMS grants and also support PKCS#11 integration to our HSM signing workflow for customers that provide an HSM endpoint. In the cross-account KMS flow, the export process writes to your account's bucket (or encrypts with your key) and we generate the manifest; the manifest can be signed with your key on a per-export basis.

Manifest & schema: attached export_sample.ndjson (3 event lines) and a small JSON Schema file embedded in the sample (fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, action, resource, request_payload_redacted(boolean), redaction_reason). When a field is redacted we include a redaction token in the manifest and a mapping table describing the redaction method (pseudonymization, truncation, hash).

Tamper-evidence options summarized:
- SHA256 checksums per file + signed manifest (Redwood HSM key)
- Detached signature (PKCS#7) for cross-checking
- Optional third-party timestamping (RFC 3161)
- Customer-key signing (KMS/HSM) on request

Delivery options & evidence: for S3 presigned deliveries we include a delivery manifest with checksums, a signed manifest file, and a chain-of-custody PDF. For physical deliveries we provide a tamper-evident seal number and signature log.

Next steps: if you approve, we can run a scoped POC export from a non-production slice (timeboxed) and deliver the package along with verification steps so your security team can validate signatures and checksum verification.

Attachments: export_sample.ndjson (ndjson), export_schema.json (json; embedded schema snippet)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Kathy — chiming in from security/ops. Happy to coordinate the pilot export and verification. Proposed next steps:

1) Scope: define a non-production slice (example: account X logs between 2024-10-01 and 2024-10-07) and a list of fields you need preserved.
2) Pilot export: Redwood will perform the export, produce NDJSON + schema + signed manifest, and deliver via a pre-agreed mechanism (S3 cross-account or SFTP).
3) Verification: provide checksums and signature verification steps; we can run through them on a call.

Operational notes: the pilot can be completed within 72 hours for a small slice. For larger datasets we'll provide a firm ETA in the export request response. We will stamp the manifest using our HSM and can demonstrate verification using your key if you'd like.

If that works, propose a 30-minute working session on Mon 2025-04-21 10:00 AM PST to finalize scope.

Thanks — Ben
